article.headline: SWIFT City: Sarjapura's Planned Tech Campus Faces Compensation Row
paragraphs: The site is in the Sarjapura Industrial Area, Sarjapur hobli, Anekal taluk, near NH 44 and NH 48. It is listed at about 23 km from Sarjapur. Connecting roads, 150 ft wide, are planned but not yet built.
The government earmarked 1,000 acres, with 8-10 plug-and-play facilities of 20-25 acres each planned. The sources opened give no investment figure, job estimate or anchor tenant.
The sources make no predictions for nearby property. Any effect would depend on the land dispute being settled and the facilities and roads being built.

article.headline: Quantum City: Big Targets, Small Site at Hesaraghatta
paragraphs: Quantum City, or Q-City, is a planned quantum technology hub at Hesaraghatta in northwest Bengaluru. The Karnataka Government is the agency, working under the Karnataka Quantum Mission. The project is at the announced stage.

The state's INR 1,000 crore Karnataka Quantum Mission is a state-level budget allocation, not a Quantum City-specific project cost. ETH Zurich and CERN are named only as partners in discussions, and global partners are still being invited.

The state targets a $20 billion quantum economy by 2035 and more than 200,000 jobs in the sector. These are sector goals, not figures for this project. No construction or funding award has been found.
The sources make no claims about nearby property. Given the small site and early stage, any local effect would depend on partners signing on and construction starting.

article.headline: KWIN City: A Knowledge Hub Still on Paper

key_facts.label: Agency
key_facts.value: Karnataka Commerce & Industries Dept (land via KIADB)

paragraphs: KWIN City, short for Knowledge, Wellbeing and Innovation City, is aimed at knowledge, health, innovation and research, according to the project descriptions. It is at the announced stage. The Karnataka Commerce & Industries Department is the agency, with land to come through KIADB.

The site lies between Dobbaspete and Doddaballapura, near the Satellite Town Ring Road. The nearest town is Doddaballapur, at a listed distance of about 36 km. Listed links include the Bengaluru-Hubballi-Mumbai rail route, NH 44 and NH 648, plus a planned central monorail with stops every 800 metres.

Today the project is an announcement rather than a built site. A search report, undated, mentions farmer protests over land acquisition around Doddaballapur. The monorail is described as planned, not funded or under construction.

The sources offer no price forecasts for nearby property. Any local expectations would rest on the announced rail, highway and ring-road links actually arriving, and on the final land area being settled.

article.headline: Harohalli Leads Race for Bengaluru's Second Airport
paragraphs: Karnataka is exploring a second greenfield airport for Bengaluru, with the Airports Authority of India (AAI) providing technical input. The project is only proposed, and no cost figure has been found.
The state government and AAI are the named parties. The sources give no investment, land area or job numbers. A feasibility report is to go to the Union government.

The project is expected to be completed by 2032-33, but the final site is to be chosen after a feasibility assessment. No final site decision has been made. A search summary of the AAI pre-feasibility report flags restricted airspace for all sites.
The sources make no price predictions. Since the site is undecided, any expectations about land near Harohalli or the other areas remain speculative.
article.standfirst: Harohalli on Kanakapura Road is the leading contender, but the site is not final and the airport is only proposed.

The project is expected to be completed by 2032-33.

It is located at Dobbaspet, Nelamangala taluk, off Tumakuru Road, a listed distance of about 50 km. No other connectivity details are given in the sources reviewed.

article.headline: Bengaluru Business Corridor: Package 1 Goes to Tender
paragraphs: The Bengaluru Business Corridor, also called the Peripheral Ring Road, is a 74 km project run by the BDA. It is split into three packages in total, and it has reached the tendered stage.

The route runs from Tumakuru Road (BIEC Madavara, near Nelamangala) to Ballari Road, then along Old Madras Road and Hosur Road. Connections include NICE Road at Madavara and a grade separator at the Hesaraghatta junction.

About 83% of Package 1 land has been acquired. Earlier tenders drew weak bidder response, and land acquisition and compensation disputes remain for the other packages. Integration with NICE Road is described as complex.
The corridor articles name no planned township nodes, and the sources make no property-price forecasts. Local expectations would depend on construction progress, which depends on bidders and land.

article.headline: BMR Plans Nine Industrial Townships Across 13,500 Acres
paragraphs: The townships would cover 13,500 acres. Individual locations are not named in the source, so where they would sit relative to Bengaluru is unknown. No connectivity details are given.
About 7,900 acres have already been acquired, the report says. No investment figure, job estimate or anchor tenant has been stated, and the report is a single source.
The plan also mentions a separate AI City on the lines of Singapore's Punggol, with land still to be identified. The report notes this is likely to raise farmer anxiety in Bidadi.
Because no township sites are named, the sources support no conclusions about nearby property. Buyers would first need the locations and timelines to be published.

article.headline: Shivaram Karanth Layout: 18,400 Sites Await Clarity
paragraphs: Dr K Shivaram Karanth Layout is a BDA layout in north Bengaluru. Its stage is unclear in the sources reviewed, which come mainly from one report. This article describes what has been reported, not a confirmed delivery schedule.

The BDA is the agency. No project cost, investment figure or jobs estimate is given. The report covers site reservation, price and the application timeline, but the sources give no firm details on them.
Allotment has faced long delays, and price revision is undecided. A search summary says a Supreme Court-appointed committee had opposed earlier allotment to farmers.
The sources make no claims about nearby property values. Prospective buyers would need clarity on pricing, legal questions and allotment dates before any conclusions.
article.standfirst: The BDA's north Bengaluru layout has 18,400 sites reserved for land-losing farmers and landowners, but price and allotment timing remain unsettled.

article.headline: BMRDA's Satellite Towns: Draft Plans, Bidadi First
paragraphs: The Bengaluru Metropolitan Region Development Authority (BMRDA) has satellite town plans for Nelamangala, Kanakapura, Magadi, Anekal and Hoskote, plus integrated townships along the Satellite Town Ring Road (STRR). The project is proposed.
Locations named along the STRR are Bidadi, Solur near Magadi, and Nandagudi near Hoskote. The nearest town is listed as Hoskote. The STRR is the only connectivity named, and no distances are given.

According to an undated Deccan Herald report, seen via a search summary, draft master plans for five satellite townships have been prepared. The sources give no area, investment figure, job estimate or anchor tenant.
The same report says Bidadi would be taken up first as a pilot. Source dates are unclear, so the timing of these plans cannot be placed. Nothing indicates approval or funding.
The sources make no predictions for nearby property. Because the plans are draft and undated, any local expectations remain speculative until approvals and timelines are published.
